title: Can You Disable Photoshop's Unified Text Engine? (Fix Hebrew Text Layouts)
excerpt: Learn why Adobe removed the option to disable the Unified Text Engine in Photoshop and how to fix broken, reversed, or disconnected Hebrew typography natively.
targetKeyword: disable unified text engine photoshop hebrew, fix hebrew text photoshop, photoshop typing backward hebrew fix, photoshop world ready composer hebrew, adobe unified text engine hebrew layout bug
content:
You cannot disable the Unified Text Engine in modern versions of Adobe Photoshop (v23.0 through Photoshop 2026). According to Adobe's official typography documentation, legacy East Asian and Middle Eastern engine toggles have been permanently integrated into a single unified core.

You do not need to downgrade or disable the engine to resolve reversed Hebrew typing, displaced Niqqud (vowels), or flipped punctuation. Rendering issues occur when default paragraph direction rules mismatch your script direction.

Quick Action Checklist: Fix Hebrew Rendering Immediately

Before modifying application preferences, run through this quick checklist on your problematic text layer:

  • Paragraph Direction: Set direction to Right-to-Left (RTL), not just Right Align.
  • Layout Composer: Activate the World-Ready Layout engine.
  • Digit Settings: Set digits to 'Default' or 'Standard' to prevent reversed inline numbers.
  • Font Selection: Ensure you are using an OpenType font with dedicated Hebrew GPOS glyph tables.
Pro Tip: Text alignment and text direction perform completely different actions. Alignment aligns the bounding box relative to the canvas margin, whereas Paragraph Direction controls the Unicode Bidirectional (BiDi) ordering of characters, periods, and numbers.

Step-by-Step: Restore Correct RTL Character Flow

Follow these steps to configure your workspace for proper Right-to-Left script evaluation across all active layers.

1. Enable Right-to-Left (RTL) Paragraph Direction

Opening legacy Western PSD templates often forces new text layers into Left-to-Right (LTR) mode by default.

  1. Highlight your Hebrew text layer using the Type Tool (T).
  2. Open the Paragraph Panel via Window → Paragraph.
  3. Click the Right-to-Left Paragraph Direction button (arrow pointing left over horizontal line icons).
  4. If the direction icons are invisible, open the Paragraph panel flyout menu (top-right hamburger icon) and check Middle Eastern Features.

2. Assign the World-Ready Layout Composer

Standard single-line composers break line wraps when Hebrew and Latin scripts interact within the same frame.

  1. Select your active text block.
  2. In the Paragraph Panel flyout menu, choose World-Ready Layout (or Adobe World-Ready Paragraph Composer).
  3. Verify that inline numbers and English words embedded in Hebrew sentences instantly drop into proper order.

If you export final vector designs for online software products or UI platforms, see our technical breakdown on exporting SVG vector assets with intact Right-to-Left glyph shaping.

3. Verify Application Language Options

Fine-tune vowel placement (Niqqud) and dictionary rules through the main application toolbar.

  1. Navigate to Type → Language Options in the main application bar.
  2. Ensure Middle Eastern Features is checked.
  3. Open the Character Panel (Window → Character) and set the dictionary language to Hebrew for precise spellchecking.

Troubleshooting Missing Options and Legacy PSD Files

If options under Type → Language Options remain grayed out, your Adobe Creative Cloud installation lacks the necessary Middle Eastern localization components.

  1. Save your work and close Photoshop completely.
  2. Open the Adobe Creative Cloud Desktop App.
  3. Click your profile icon → Preferences → Apps.
  4. Change Default Install Language to English (Supports Hebrew).
  5. Relaunch Photoshop to automatically initialize missing international typography definitions.
Pro Tip: For complex cross-platform workflows involving external script processing or web handoffs, review our guide on fixing complex script rendering across Photoshop, Figma, and server-side pipelines.

Recommended Hebrew-Compatible OpenType Fonts

Outdated TrueType (.ttf) files compiled before modern Unicode BiDi standards will misalign Niqqud vowels regardless of engine settings. Standardize your design system using reliable OpenType alternatives:

  • Google Fonts (Open Source): Assistant, Rubik, Heebo, Varela Round, Frank Ruhl Libre.
  • Adobe Fonts Collection: Miriam Libre, Taamey Ashkenaz, Noto Sans Hebrew.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why does my Hebrew text still type backward after turning on RTL?

This happens when the Paragraph Composer remains set to standard Western single-line layout. Switch the composer setting to World-Ready Layout inside the Paragraph panel flyout menu to restore correct script ordering.

How do I stop punctuation marks from jumping to the wrong end of a sentence?

Sentence-ending punctuation flips to the wrong side when your layer uses LTR paragraph direction instead of RTL. Change the paragraph direction button in the Paragraph panel to Right-to-Left.

Will changing Creative Cloud install language to English (Supports Hebrew) change my UI?

No, your primary menus and toolbar labels will remain in English. It simply installs background typography components necessary to parse Bidirectional text scripts properly.

Why are my Hebrew Niqqud (vowel points) overlapping with main letters?

Overlapping Niqqud indicates that your current font lacks modern OpenType GPOS positioning tables. Switch your font family to a modern web-ready option such as Heebo, Assistant, or Rubik.
